title: Fetch-based registration submit (ISS-374/373 fix) is unproved in a real browser and replaces native form navigation
evidence: register_form now POSTs via fetch(redirect:'error', mode:'no-cors') from one synchronous validated snapshot instead of HTMLFormElement.submit(). Proven only against a fake DOM/fetch under node and a mocked Python seam; no Chrome was launched (shared CPU). Page no longer navigates after submit; response body is opaque so only 'request completed' is known.
fix_direction: Run test_sb_join_iframe.py::test_registration_actual_local_form_and_safety_exceptions (real Chrome, 307/308 loop already updated to expect a single /submit POST) when the Chrome worker is idle; checker decides whether CDP Fetch request-stage interception (ledger fix_direction for ISS-374) is still required on top, and whether service-worker observation is covered by Network.setBypassServiceWorker.

title: Offline registration suite has no static unapproved-target case; removing the target host check, or credentials:'include', leaves all 15 tests green
evidence: Checker mutations on sb_join.py REGISTRATION_JS: dropping the target-host test (`!i.allowedHosts.includes(target.hostname)`) -> 15 passed; credentials:'include' -> 'omit' -> 15 passed. All ISS-373 cases mutate AFTER validation, so the static-bad-action path (action/formaction to unapproved host, protocol-relative, userinfo, other port/scheme) is only exercised by the real-Chrome test. Checker probe against the unmutated code refused all of these correctly (evil.example, //evil.example, 127.0.0.1@evil.example, user:p@, LOCALHOST, :50701, https), so this is a coverage gap, not a leak.
fix_direction: Add parametrized harness cases with scenario.formAction / button formaction set to those URLs expecting action_required/redirect_host and zero posts; assert fetch opts.credentials == 'include' and Content-Type header in the clean case.
